title: Displacement magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the net displacement (1.0 m) using areas under the v-t graph, accounting for positive and negative contributions.

title: Total distance traveled
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly calculate the total distance (1.25 m) using the sum of absolute areas under the v-t graph.

title: Inclination angle
description: Essential Criteria: The student must determine the correct angle of inclination (53°) from the accelerations on the incline.

title: Pulling force magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must determine the correct magnitude of the pulling force (36 N) using Newton's second law on the incline.

title: Acceleration from graph
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly compute the three accelerations (6 m/s², 12 m/s², 4 m/s²) from the slopes of the v-t graph segments.

title: Force analysis on incline
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply Newton's second law separately for the upward pull phase and the coasting phases to relate acceleration to forces.

title: Time interval identification
description: Optional Criteria: The student may explicitly identify the time intervals (0–0.5 s, 0.5–0.75 s, 0.75–1 s) corresponding to different motion phases.

title: Sign error in displacement
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student treats the negative velocity area as positive when computing displacement, failing to subtract it.

title: Confusing distance and displacement
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses the same method for distance and displacement, not taking absolute values for distance.
